title: Now Google says it might use your Gmail and Google Photos data to target ads
slides: Google might use your Gmail to target ads — worried?
It cites a policy update covering Photos and Gmail
But ads were never actually trained on your content before
You can opt out in settings, but defaults stay on
Check your ad settings today before it expands
thread_text:
1. Your Gmail ads worry?

Google just updated its policy to cover Photos and Gmail, but ads were never trained on your content before. So why the change now?

2. Policy update explained

The new terms explicitly mention Photos and Gmail, but Google says it's just housekeeping. Yet the timing raises eyebrows.

3. Ads never trained on content

Before this update, Google didn't use your emails or photos to train ad algorithms. Now the door is open, even if they say it's not.

4. Opt out, defaults stay on

You can turn off ad personalization in settings, but the default is still on. Most users won't even notice the change.

5. Check your settings now

Open your Google account, go to Ad Settings, and decide if you're comfortable. Do it before the policy expands further.
